zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly ties an attribute to a specific house number, place that attribute in that house right away.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house index (e.g., "Eric is in the first house" or "the Samsung phone is in the second house").
zebralogic.example: Leaving a fixed‑position clue unassigned and later trying to infer the position indirectly.

zebralogic.title: Translate direct adjacency into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: Clues using "directly left of" or "directly right of" impose an exact offset of one house between the two referenced entities.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of", even if embedded in a longer sentence.
zebralogic.example: Treating a "directly left of" clue as only an ordering and not enforcing adjacency.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating "N houses between X and Y" means the absolute positional difference between X and Y is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses separating two entities.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "2 houses between X and Y" as a distance of 2 houses instead of the required 3.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two (or more) attributes, they must be assigned to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue links attributes with words like "is", "the same as", or "the person who ... is also ...".
zebralogic.example: Assigning linked attributes from an equivalence clue to different houses.

zebralogic.title: Treat "somewhere left/right of" as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere to the left/right of Y only impose an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase "somewhere left of" or "somewhere right of" without the word "directly".
zebralogic.example: Assuming "Alice is somewhere left of Bob" means Alice must be immediately left of Bob.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: If a clue forbids an attribute from a particular house (e.g., "Bob is not in house 4"), record that exclusion immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a negation about a specific house.
zebralogic.example: Placing an entity in a house that a clue explicitly forbids.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once; after assigning a value to a house, remove it from the pool for other houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, after any assignment.
zebralogic.example: Using the same phone model for two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values across categories
zebralogic.principle: When a term appears in more than one attribute category, keep the categories separate and never mix them.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a value that could belong to multiple categories (e.g., a name that is also a child name).
zebralogic.example: Treating the child named Alice as the mother named Alice.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Attribute values must be output exactly as they appear in the problem statement, including capitalization.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "alice" instead of the required "Alice" for a name.

zebralogic.title: Interpret "next to each other" as bidirectional adjacency
zebralogic.principle: Clues stating that two entities are "next to each other" indicate they occupy adjacent houses, with no fixed direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase "next to each other" (or synonyms).
zebralogic.example: Assuming "X next to Y" means X must be left of Y, ignoring the possibility that Y could be left of X.

zebralogic.description: Treating "somewhere left of" as adjacency (directly left)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the weaker ordering phrase with the stronger adjacency phrase, assuming the entities must be adjacent.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "somewhere left/right of" only imposes an ordering; use the adjacency skill only for "directly left/right of".

zebralogic.description: Interpreting "N houses between" as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets to add one to the count, treating the number of intervening houses as the total distance.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says "N houses between X and Y", enforce that |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, placing them in different houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates attributes, assign them together to the same house before proceeding.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may duplicate a value across houses, especially when many constraints are present.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain a pool of unused values for each category and remove a value as soon as it is assigned.

zebralogic.description: Assuming a fixed direction for "next to each other" clues
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets "next to each other" as implying a left‑right order, rather than symmetric adjacency.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat "next to each other" as bidirectional adjacency; either entity can be on the left.
